content: Citation hallucination is measured at 56% of AI-generated citations containing errors, 1 in 5 fully hallucinated (Resnik 2026, peer-reviewed); persists even in peer-reviewed proceedings (arXiv phantom references); arXiv now bans authors for unchecked fabricated references. Most dangerous mode (Haqq.ai legal analysis): a REAL citation attached to WRONG content, delivered confidently - this is what caused court sanctions (Mata v Avianca pattern). Mitigations: only cite from retrieved/verified sources (never model memory), verify every citation against an authoritative database, human-in-loop review before output.
